title: Uncapped desiredAPYBps converts directly into unbounded phUSD mint pressure; the two-step gate is delay-only
description: setDesiredAPY is onlyOwner with a two-step preview/commit gate (100-block delay), but has no on-chain magnitude bound on bps. SYMBOLIC-005 PASS confirms the gate state machine works exactly as designed — it provides a 100-block delay and nothing more. Because phUSD is both stake and reward, an arbitrarily large APY converts directly into an arbitrarily large per-second phUSD mint flow. The owner can pre-stake, hike APY, then accrue and exit with freshly-minted phUSD with only ~20 minutes of mempool friction.
impact: Owner can set arbitrary APY; combined with phUSD being both stake and reward, an adversarial owner can pre-stake -> hike APY -> claim -> exit, with only a ~20-minute friction window. Affects phUSD supply system-wide. The structural critique is that the gate's design intent (mitigate magnitude attacks) is not actually realized — the gate is delay-only.
attackPath: Owner waits <=100 blocks, calls setDesiredAPY(huge_value) — commit.
Time passes; owner accrues phUSD via _claimRewards.
Owner withdraws + claims, extracting freshly-minted phUSD.
likelihood: depends on owner trust; the function is onlyOwner-gated
recommendation: Add a hard magnitude cap: require(bps <= MAX_APY_BPS) where MAX_APY_BPS reflects the protocol's economic envelope (e.g., 10_000 = 100%). Optionally extend the commit window from 100 blocks to a time-based delay (e.g., 24h) and route the setter through a timelock. The current gate is a delay-only design — converting it into a delay + magnitude-bound design is a minimal-code, high-value hardening.

symbolic: SYMBOLIC-005 PASS (two-step gate state-machine proven correct — gate provides exactly the 100-block delay and nothing more)

classifierRationale: onlyOwner; gate exists (two-step). Magnitude critique is structural but trigger is admin action. Routes to C.
